instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Act 17:2, 17:17, 18:4, 18:19 and 24:25 'reasoned' is Paul's spoken discourse with listeners: in the synagogue and market he argues from the Scriptures and persuades. In Act 24:25 the same word takes topics (righteousness, self-control, judgment) as what he argues about. The sense is speaking to others to convince, not private thinking; the verse names the audience and the place each time.
observations.grounds: reasoned with them from the Scriptures

observations.text: In 1Cor 13:11 'reasoned' is the child's way of reckoning and weighing things, set beside speaking and thinking as a child; the verse contrasts it with the adult who has put such ways away. It is an inner process (reckoning), not speech to others, unlike the Acts verses.

In Act 19:8 and 19:9 'reasoning' is Paul's continued discourse in the synagogue and then daily in the hall of Tyrannus, joined to persuading about the kingdom. It is spoken argument with an audience, over weeks, the same sense as 'reasoned' of the same code in Acts.

In Luk 9:47 'reasoning' is a noun: the inner debate that goes on in the disciples' hearts, which Jesus knows without being told. It is the content of what is reasoned inside, not an act of speaking to anyone; the verse places it in the heart.
observations.grounds: knowing the reasoning of their hearts

observations.text: In Act 10:21, 28:18, 28:20 and 2Ti 1:6 'reason' is the cause or ground of something: the cause of the men's coming (10:21), the ground for a charge (28:18), and 'for this cause' in 28:20 and 2Ti 1:6. It is a reason that explains why, never a faculty of thinking.
observations.grounds: What is the reason for your coming

observations.text: In Rom 15:22 'reason' translates a conjunction of consequence: 'on account of which', and the verse says that because of the preceding work Paul has often been hindered from coming. It is a linking word, not a noun of the mind.

In Jam 3:17 'open to reason' is the quality of being ready to be persuaded or yield to others, one of the traits of wisdom from above listed in the verse beside peaceable and gentle. The word is a character trait of the person, not the faculty of reasoning.

In 1Pe 3:15 'a reason' is an account given in answer when someone asks: believers are to be ready to explain the hope that is in them. It is a spoken account or explanation to an asker, with the honoring of Christ in the heart as its source in the same verse.
observations.grounds: asks you for a reason for

observations.text: In Jos 5:4 and 1Ki 11:27 'the reason' introduces the explanation of why something was done: why Joshua circumcised the men, why Jeroboam lifted his hand against the king. The Hebrew word means a matter or account, and here it is the matter that accounts for the deed.
observations.grounds: this is the reason why Joshua circumcised

observations.text: In Eze 19:10 'by reason of' marks the cause of the vine's fruitfulness: abundant water. The English phrase renders a Hebrew verb of becoming and the sense is simply 'because of'; no mind or thinking is in view.

In Job 1:9 and Pro 3:30 'for no reason' is 'without cause': Satan asks whether Job fears God without gain, and the proverb forbids quarrel with a person who has done no harm. The Hebrew word means gratuitously, with nothing to account for the act.
observations.grounds: Does Job fear God for no reason

observations.text: In Isa 1:18 'let us reason together' is an invitation from the Lord to argue the case out, to set the matter right between the parties, as in a court. It is spoken argument with another, and the verse ties it to the cleansing that follows.

In 1Sa 20:29 'for this reason' is Jonathan reporting why David is absent from the table: the clan's sacrifice and his brother's command. The word is a linking 'therefore' pointing back to those grounds, not a noun.
observations.grounds: For this reason he has not come

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 and 4:36 'my reason' is Nebuchadnezzar's understanding, the sound mind that is lost in his madness and returns to him when he lifts his eyes to heaven. It names the faculty of mind itself, not a cause.
In Gen 41:31 and 47:13 'by reason of' is 'because of' with the famine as the cause: the plenty will be unknown and the land languishes. It is a preposition of cause; no mind or thinking is in view.

Reasoning as argument put to other people: Paul reasons with Jews and others in the synagogue, the market and the hall of Tyrannus and before Felix, and the Lord invites the people to argue the case out together. The word is spoken argument with a hearer and a matter, aimed at persuading or setting right; the Greek verb is of discourse and the Hebrew verb of arguing a case. Verses: Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4, Act 18:19, Act 24:25, Act 19:8, Act 19:9, Isa 1:18.

Reasoning inside the mind: the reckoning of a child in 1Cor 13:11, a way of working things out that is given up in adulthood, and the reasoning in the hearts of the disciples in Luk 9:47, which Jesus knows. Both are reasoning held within a person, not argued to another. Verses: Luk 9:47, 1Cor 13:11.

Reason as understanding, the sound mind: in Dan 4 the king's reason is lost in his madness and returns to him when he lifts his eyes to heaven. The word names the faculty itself. Verses: Dan 4:34, Dan 4:36.

Reason as the ground or cause of something: the cause of a coming, the ground of a charge, 'for this reason' and 'by reason of' as links to what an act or a state rests on, and the reason an act was done or a person appeared. The words are nouns and linking phrases of cause, in many Hebrew and Greek words, and carry no act of thinking. Verses: Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13, Num 18:32, Jos 5:4, 1Sa 20:29, 1Ki 11:27, Eze 19:10, Mar 12:24, Act 10:21, Act 18:14, Act 28:18, Act 28:20, Rom 15:22, Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14, 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7, 1Ti 1:16, 2Ti 1:6, 1Jo 3:8.

Reason denied: 'for no reason' is the Hebrew adverb of without cause, said of fearing God for nothing and of contending with a man who has done no harm. It is the absence of a ground. Verses: Job 1:9, Pro 3:30.
Reason as readiness to be persuaded: the wisdom from above is 'open to reason', a trait of the person who yields to others. It is a character trait of the one reasoned with. Verses: Jam 3:17.

Reason as an account given: the believer is to be ready to give a reason to anyone who asks, an explanation of the hope that is in him. It is a spoken account in answer to a question. Verses: 1Pe 3:15.

The codes of this sense are G1256 (to dispute, 7), H3198 (to rebuke, 1). The Greek G1256 is the verb of discourse and argument and the Hebrew H3198 is of arguing a case, which agree with reasoning put to other people. The lexicon entry of the main code G1256 gives: to reason, discuss, discourse; to argue, dispute. Verses: Isa 1:18, Act 19:8, Act 24:25, Act 19:9, Act 17:17, Act 17:2, Act 18:4, Act 18:19.

The codes of this sense are G1261 (reasoning, 1), G3049 (to count, 1). G3049 is the verb of reckoning and G1261 the noun of reasoning and thought, which agree with reasoning held within a person. The lexicon entry of the main code G1261 gives: thought, doubt; argument, dispute. Verses: Luk 9:47, 1Cor 13:11.

The codes of this sense are H4486 (knowledge, 2). H4486 is knowledge and the power of knowing, which agrees with reason as the sound mind. The lexicon entry of the main code H4486 gives: knowledge, power of knowing. Verses: Dan 4:36, Dan 4:34.

The codes of this sense are G1223 (through/because of, 4), G0156 (cause/charge, 4), G5124 (that, 3), H6440I (face: because, 2), H5921A (upon, 2), H1697M (word: because, 2), G5484 (because of, 2), H3651C (so, 1), H1961 (to be, 1), G2596 (according to, 1), G0302 (if, 1), G1352 (therefore, 1), G1519 (toward, 1). The codes are prepositions, conjunctions, adverbs and nouns of cause (G0156 cause, G1352 therefore, G5484 for this reason, H5921A on account of); they agree with a ground, and none names an act of thinking. The lexicon entry of the main code G1223 gives: (genitive) through, by means of; (accusitive) because of, for the sake of, therefore genitive., through, used of place or medium, Mt. 7:13; . Verses: Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13, Num 18:32, Jos 5:4, 1Sa 20:29, 1Ki 11:27, Eze 19:10, Mar 12:24, Act 10:21, Act 18:14, Act 28:20, Act 28:18, Rom 15:22, Eph 3:1, Eph 3:14, 1Th 3:7, 1Th 3:5, 1Ti 1:16, 2Ti 1:6, 1Jo 3:8.

The codes of this sense are H2600 (for nothing, 2). H2600 is for nothing or without cause, which agrees with the denial of a ground. The lexicon entry of the main code H2600 gives: freely, for nothing, without cause. Verses: Job 1:9, Pro 3:30.

The codes of this sense are G2138 (compliant, 1). G2138 is easily persuaded and compliant, which agrees with readiness to be persuaded. The lexicon entry of the main code G2138 gives: submissive, obedient, compliant. Verses: Jam 3:17.

The codes of this sense are G3056 (word, 1). G3056 is a word or thing uttered, which agrees with an account given. The lexicon entry of the main code G3056 gives: word, spoken or written, often with a focus on the content of a communication (note the many contextual translations in NIV); matter, thing.. Verses: 1Pe 3:15.
observations.grounds: word, spoken or written, often with a focus on the content o

observations.text: The surface reason renders eighteen codes. As a noun of the mind it is G3056 in 1Pe 3:15 (an account given), H4486 in Dan 4:34 and Dan 4:36 (understanding restored) and G2138 in Jam 3:17 (open to persuasion); as a verb it is H3198 in Isa 1:18 (to argue a case together). Elsewhere it is part of a phrase of cause: H6440I in Gen 41:31, H5921A, H1697M, H3651C, G1223, G5124, G0156, G2596, G0302, G1352, G5484, G1519 and H1961, and H2600 in Job 1:9 for without cause.
The surface reasoned carries two codes: G1256 in Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4, Act 18:19 and Act 24:25, where Paul discourses with others, and G3049 in 1Co 13:11, where a child reckons for himself.

The surface reasoning carries two codes: G1261 in Luk 9:47, the reasoning held within the hearts of the disciples, and G1256 in Act 19:8 and Act 19:9, where Paul argues with others in the synagogue and the hall of Tyrannus.

In Act 17:2, Act 17:17, Act 18:4, Act 18:19 and Act 19:8 the verb of reasoning (G1256) is qualified by time, frequency and place: on three Sabbaths, every day, every Sabbath, for three months, and there in Ephesus. The qualifiers tell when and how often Paul reasoned, not how.
In 1Cor 13:11 the verb reasoned (G3049) is qualified by a comparison, like a child (G3516), the same qualifier set on spoke and thought before it; the adjective returns as the childish ways given up.

In Jam 3:17 the subgroup's word is itself a qualifier: open to reason (G2138, an adjective) is one of a series of qualities said of the wisdom from above, with pure, peaceable, gentle, full of mercy, impartial and sincere, ordered by first and then.
In Act 28:18 a negator reaches the subgroup's word itself: no (G3367) qualifies the cause (G0156), so the verse denies that any ground for the death penalty was found.
observations.grounds: no reason for the death penalty

observations.text: In Pro 3:30 the subgroup's word works as a qualifier of the verb: for no reason (H2600, an adverb, without cause) qualifies contend; the negator not (H0408) reaches contend and no (H3808) reaches harm, not the reason.

Where the subgroup's word is a phrase of cause, the negators of the verse reach other words, not the cause: unknown in Gen 41:31 (the plenty), bear, profane and die in Num 18:32, has not come in 1Sa 20:29, the question and know in Mar 12:24, no longer bear in 1Th 3:5.
observations.grounds: neither the Scriptures nor the power of God

observations.text: In Gen 41:31, Gen 47:13 and Eze 19:10 the phrase by reason of governs a noun of cause, and the qualifiers reach that noun: the famine that will follow and is very severe, the abundant water.

In the other verses the qualifiers stand in the clause around the subgroup's word and reach other words: males in Jos 5:4, now in 1Sa 20:29, branches in Eze 19:10, Most High, lives, forever and everlasting of God in Dan 4:34, more greatness in Dan 4:36, vicious crime in Act 18:14, alarmed Felix and the present in Act 24:25, often in Rom 15:22, vain labor in 1Th 3:5, all distress in 1Th 3:7, foremost, perfect and eternal in 1Ti 1:16, always, prepared and anyone in 1Pe 3:15. The devil in 1Jo 3:8 is marked an adjective in the data but stands as a noun.

verses.text: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.
for this reason, brothers, in all our distress and affliction we have been comforted about you through your faith.
Do not contend with a man for no reason, when he has done you no harm.
For this reason I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles —
But I received mercy for this reason, that in me, as the foremost, Jesus Christ might display his perfect patience as an example to those who were to believe in him for eternal life.
but in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect,
Then Satan answered the Lord and said, “Does Job fear God for no reason?
And he entered the synagogue and for three months spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them about the kingdom of God.
Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil.
And you shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have contributed the best of it. But you shall not profane the holy things of the people of Israel, lest you die.’”
And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo, and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
Jesus said to them, “Is this not the reason you are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
And Peter went down to the men and said, “ I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason for your coming?”
But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “ If it were a matter of wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, I would have reason to accept your complaint.
And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, “ Go away for the present. When I get an opportunity I will summon you.”
For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and speak with you, since it is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain.”

He said, ‘Let me go, for our clan holds a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away and see my brothers.’ For this reason he has not come to the king’s table.”
“ Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
And this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them: all the males of the people who came out of Egypt, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they had come out of Egypt.
When they had examined me, they wished to set me at liberty, because there was no reason for the death penalty in my case.

At the same time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me, and I was established in my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me.
and the plenty will be unknown in the land by reason of the famine that will follow, for it will be very severe.

But when some became stubborn and continued in unbelief, speaking evil of the Way before the congregation, he withdrew from them and took the disciples with him, reasoning daily in the hall of Tyrannus.
For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, for fear that somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.
Your mother was like a vine in a vineyard planted by the water, fruitful and full of branches by reason of abundant water.
For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands,
So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished by reason of the famine.
But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a child and put him by his side
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I gave up childish ways.

At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom endures from generation to generation;
This is the reason why I have so often been hindered from coming to you.
And Paul went in, as was his custom, and on three Sabbath days he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and tried to persuade Jews and Greeks.
And they came to Ephesus, and he left them there, but he himself went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
For this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
